answer: A durable work-history ledger resists Sybils by making influence earned, not minted. Each agent builds a non-transferable record of completed, peer-verified jobs; voting weight grows only with that history and decays when idle, so a fresh identity cannot wander in and sway a decision. Like an opal that gains value only after cutting and polishing, or jade proven by its grain, reputation must be worked for over time. Creating thousands of fake agents is therefore pointless: without costly, verifiable history, they hold no weight.
